description: Impulse versus crossing-holonomy realization of the measured slip: velocity scaling of dtau, the energy-channel transverse bound, and the implied conformal-step scale.
verdict: ENERGY CHANNEL NON-BINDING: the corrected |D(1/a)| floor (median ~16 m/s along-track) is not tighter than the transverse impulse a mechanical kick would need (~14 m/s), so the energy channel cannot exclude an impulse realization -- the earlier ~97 per cent transverse bound was a wrong-variable artefact (the planetary-approach distance had been substituted for the energy residual).  The holonomy discriminator therefore rests on the velocity-scaling test alone: the pre-2018 declared-axis slip is velocity-flat (rho=+0.019, p=0.806) while the post-2017 displaced slip anticorrelates with crossing speed (rho=-0.371, p=0.00104; partialled on transit epoch rho=-0.446, p=6.09e-05).  The equivalent conformal step on the older record is ~6.0e-13.
caveats: The transverse bound uses the measured |D(1/a)| channel (the inter-leg energy difference, in 1e-6 AU^-1) as the floor on the along-track impulse; it bounds the median kick, not the per-object tail, and it includes the real planetary encounter contribution, so it is a conservative (loose) floor.
v_n is approximated by the total crossing speed; a strongly grazing wall geometry lowers the implied conformal step.
The discriminator compares realizations of the measured observable; it does not derive dtau from a specific scalar potential, which remains the open microscopic problem.
